hints: Focus on the type of bonding around each carbon, since hybridisation is decided by sigma bonds plus lone pairs, or more simply by single, double and triple bonds.
Pick out every carbon with a double bond first, remembering that a C=C carbon has three sigma regions and is sp2.
Check the cumulated C=C=C unit carefully and the C-C triple bond, then count only the carbons with exactly one double bond plus two singles to finish the total.
walkthrough:
**Recall the hybridisation rule**

Think simply. A carbon with 4 single bonds is sp3, with one double bond is sp2, and with a triple bond or two double bonds is sp.

Rule to use:
$$\text{steric number} = \text{sigma bonds + lone pairs on carbon}$$

**Map the skeleton of Q**

Count the carbons. There are 10 carbons in total. From left to right the main chain is $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}=\text{C}=\text{C}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3$ with a methyl branch and a $\text{-CH=CH}_2$ branch.

This helps you look at each carbon one by one.

**Identify the sp3 and sp carbons to exclude**

The three $\text{CH}_3$ groups (left end, branch on C2, right end) each have four single bonds, so they are sp3. The two $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ carbons each have a triple bond, so they are sp. The central carbon of $\text{C=C=C}$ has two double bonds, so it is also sp.

**Count the sp2 carbons**

The carbons left with exactly one double bond are: the left $\text{C=C}$ carbon (joined to two $\text{CH}_3$ groups), the right $\text{C=C}$ carbon (joined to the vinyl group and the triple bond), and the two carbons of the $\text{CH=CH}_2$ side group.

That gives:
$$1 + 1 + 2 = 4 \text{ sp}^2 \text{ carbons}$$

options.A: 3 misses one sp2 carbon. Students often count the two main-chain C=C carbons plus only one of the side-chain alkene carbons, forgetting that both carbons in CH=CH2 are sp2.
options.B: 4 is correct. Two sp2 carbons come from the cumulated diene ends (C2 and C4) and two come from the ethenyl side chain (CH=CH2). All other carbons are sp3 (CH3 groups) or sp (C triple C and central allene C).
options.C: 7 is too high. This comes from counting the central allene C=C=C carbon and the two C triple C carbons as sp2. In fact a carbon with two double bonds or one triple bond has only two sigma regions and is sp hybridised.
options.D: 10 counts every carbon as sp2. This ignores hybridisation completely and assumes all carbons in a hydrocarbon are the same, forgetting the clear difference between single, double and triple bond regions.
